properties.description: A Grade II listed art deco theatre in the heart of London. Built in 1929, this stylish building has had a varied and colourful history as a cinema, variety hall and music venue, as well as its original and current life as a theatre.
properties.name: Dominion Theatre

properties.description: The Hall stands on land which was bought in 1922: construction work, which was undertaken by Holland, Hannen & Cubitts, started that year and the Hall was opened on 17 June 1925. Decorated in the Arts & Crafts style, and resplendent with art and treasures, visitors will gain access to areas not normally open to the public and will be guided by real Company members.
properties.name: Ironmongers' Hall

properties.description: Wren's own and 'finest City Church'.  Fantastic architecture with different shapes,  twelve Corinthian columns and covered by huge dome - first of its type. Central stone altar by Henry Moore installed in 1987. Birthplace of the Samaritans.
properties.name: The City Churches: St Stephen Walbrook

properties.description: The world's oldest active biological society. Founded in 1788, the Society takes its name from the Swedish naturalist Carl Linnaeus whose botanical, zoological and library collections have been in its keeping since 1829.
properties.name: Burlington House: Linnean Society of London

properties.description: Splendid Baroque exterior. Interior destroyed in the Blitz and rebuilt to new design by Martin Bailey in 1963.

images.title: Photo of St George in the East

properties.description: A stunning cathedral in the heart of London. Discover the story of a forgotten masterpiece. Designed by Augustus Pugin and opened in 1848, the original cathedral was hailed as England's foremost Catholic church before an incendiary bomb devastated the building in 1941. Explore the history, architecture and legacy that shaped the Cathedral you see today—and discover its remarkable story.
properties.name: St George's Cathedral

properties.description: During Open House, the Friends of Battersea Parish Church present a Floral Festival, organ recitals, historical displays, alongside 3 talks exploring history, creativity, sanctuary & Battersea’s radical past. Sat 12 Sept Dr. Peter Rumley at 6pm, Tues 15 Guy Stagg at 6.30pm,  Thurs 17 at 6.30pm Rory Walsh & Mike Squires.  Plus Join us for Choral Evensong amidst the flowers at St Mary’s Battersea.

Photo of St Mary's Church, Battersea

During the Festival there will be opportunities to self-guide or to join a group tour which will include access to restricted areas such as the crypt and tower. These last about 30 min and will start on each hour with the last starting at 3 pm

properties.description:
The Wiener Holocaust Library is one of the world’s leading and most extensive archives on the Holocaust. 
From 1939 to 1945, 20 million individuals were exploited as slave and forced labourers by the Nazi regime. Our latest exhibition 'Nazi Slave Labour: Perpetrators and Victims' explores how perpetrators profited off and exploited slave labourers, alongside the first-hand stories of the victims.
properties.name: Wiener Holocaust Library

properties.description: St Anne's Limehouse has been described as 'the finest parish church in England.' Designed by Nicholas Hawksmoor, it is Grade I listed and one of the Major Churches in the Church of England. It is home to a thriving Christian congregation.

Photo of St Anne's Church, Limehouse

properties.description: Loughborough Pearson's red brick building is unimposing from the outside, but inside is a riot of Gothic Revival design. Golden mosaics reveal the character of the Grade II* listed chapel, built as part of the Middlesex Hospital.
properties.name: Fitzrovia Chapel

properties.description: Explore the Building Centre, a landmark home for architecture and the built environment in the heart of London. Discover its distinctive modernist spaces, public galleries and exhibitions, and learn how the building has brought together architects, designers, makers and city-shapers for more than 90 years.
properties.name: The Building Centre

properties.description: A floating acoustic architecture, playfully reframing public space as an essential community engagement through sound & site mapping. Accessed by smartphone, headphones & echoes.xyz app, the Pavilion is located outside the Serpentine Gallery,. Drawing on Oskar & Zofia Hansen’s Open Form architectural concept it is one of 15 in a series including Venice, Berlin, Dublin, Bergen and Arctic Norway.

We have applied circular economy principles to the retrofit of our own studio, gallery and café space on Mare Street, reducing waste, reusing materials, and designing for longevity.  Through our public exhibition and event programme we place the creative ‘act’ of architecture onto the high street.

properties.description: The Grade I listed North Wing at St Bartholomew’s Hospital in the City of London houses two of England’s most important interiors, the Great Hall, and the Hogarth Stair with its large paintings by William Hogarth. The hospital was designed by architect James Gibbs and construction of the North Wing was completed in 1732.
properties.name: St Bartholomew's Hospital

properties.description: A Gothic revival church of cathedral proportions completed in 1906 by Temple Moore with Italian baroque features from Bologna and Florence. properties.description:
Shaftesbury Hall is a Tin Tabernacle  rebuilt by North London Samaritans in 2018 to replicate the original Hall built in the 1890s.
It has been owned by North London Samaritans for 50 years and since the rebuild is used as a Community Hub, with our branch of Samaritans at the rear.
properties.name: Shaftesbury Hall

properties.description: The Croydon Urban Room is a space to talk about the past, present and future of the Croydon town centre. Through conversa­tions, stories, exhibitions and events, the Urban Room brings together the views of those who live, work and visit the area to create a shared vision of the future and test new uses live in action.
properties.name: Croydon Urban Room

Explore a history of innovative public housing developments in one of the most densely populated parts of London and end at New River Head, a striking example of public utility architecture now being repurposed for arts and culture.
properties.name: Islington New River walking tour

We have a rich history of Church Music, beautiful worship and  vestments.  We also have a passion for  social justice within our community.  We were the first parish in Edmonton Diocese to have a woman vicar.

Broadcasting 24/7 on 104.4 FM, DAB, and online, it offers over 100 weekly shows created by volunteer engineers and programme-makers. The station champions free expression and artistic diversity, providing a platform for local and international voices across arts & culture.

properties.description: Working, sleeping, playing – the City of London is home to all sorts of activities after dark. This walking tour will explore buildings and spaces, well known and lesser-known, in darkness, and will tell the history of night-time in London. We will visit places where London works, sleeps and plays at night, and over the course of two hours will even see how night time activity shifts.
properties.name: The City at night

properties.description: Grade II Listed.   Designed by Adrian Gilbert Scott.  Cruciform shape (120 feet by 120 feet) of steel girder and brick construction. Its Lantern tower – based on Ely Cathedral – is supported on parabolic arches 35 feet wide and 50 feet high.  The Stained Glass Windows were designed by John Wilson of Edinburgh and the Stations of the Cross  carved in Blue Horton Stone by Peter Watts.

properties.description: The Purpose of Light, Misan Harriman’s landmark photographic exhibition, bears witness to significant  moments, not with judgment or ideology, but with a deep and unflinching empathy for the human condition. Featuring 110 unique photographs, this exhibition is a call not for division, but for togetherness.

properties.description: As part of the Open House Festival, Streatham Hill Theatre stands out as a significant example of London’s theatrical heritage. Built in 1928–29, it was the final theatre designed by renowned architect W. G. R. Sprague. Opening in 1929, the venue hosted theatre, opera, ballet and variety performances until 1962, with a temporary closure between 1944 and 1950 due to wartime bomb damage.
properties.name: Streatham Hill Theatre

properties.description:
The building of Worlds End Studios started life as a factory manufacturing machines for commercial baking ovens; it burned down and the remains were used as the foundations of what we know today.
Two young architects found the ruined site in 1974. They wanted to create a community workspace geared toward designers, one of the first of its kind, in London.
properties.name: Worlds End Studios

properties.description: Buried treasures, banks and bullion…. Explore the legendary wealth of the City of London and its modern-day reputation as a global centre of finance. They used to say its streets were paved with gold... This guided walk explores the historic sources of the City's money, including livery companies, global trade and the development of the banking industry, and some of the ways that manifests today.
properties.name: Money, Money, Money

properties.description: This guided tour will examine the traditional roofs of Hampstead Garden Suburb. These roofs were designed by early twentieth century architects, seeking to revitalise the centuries-old tradition of English roofing crafts largely lost during the process of industrialisation. By looking up, we will discover the quirky nature of heritage roofs and the conservation challenges they pose today.

images.title: Photo of Traditional Roofing in Hampstead Garden Suburb

properties.description: Freud Museum London is the final home of the founder of psychoanalysis, Sigmund Freud, where he and his family moved to flee Nazi persecution in 1938. Freud's famous study has been preserved as he left it upon his death in 1939, while the rest of the home has been carefully transformed into a Museum celebrating the life and work of Sigmund and his daughter Anna, a pioneering child psychologist.
properties.name: Freud Museum London

properties.description: Discover Tooting’s transformation from rural village to vibrant town. Starting at Tooting Bec and following the ancient Roman Stane Street, this one-mile tour contrasts historic views with today's high street. Explore iconic building facades, changing shops, and post-war migration. See how planning has shaped the area and what the future holds for this evolving neighborhood.

The Heritage Lottery Fund, local artists, and academics are working with the church to engage and preserve how we work together as 'commoners' and 'caretakers for the 'common good'. Explore this in the Exhibition - On Common Ground - and become part of St Thomas' Future for the Common Good.

This tour ends with a tour of Tipping Point East - a new circular economy hub.

properties.description: For centuries the South Bank of the Thames sat outside the historic City of London's jurisdiction — and beyond its moral gaze. The Battle of Britain Lace Panel has recently been installed.

This tour explores a time when the area served as London’s notorious red-light district, focusing on the lives of those forced into illicit trades or marginalized by the stringent moral laws of the day. The walk will share the stories of those who lived, worked and played in the area in days gone by.

It will also look at some of the Jewish people living as Christians between these times and the key contributions Jews have made to many of the key landmarks in London  as well as England's political life.

properties.description: Hear about the history of Soho on a walk around some of the sites associated with colourful characters of yesteryear. From Soho's beginnings as a fashionable suburb in the seventeenth century up to the 1950s, I regale you with delicious snippets of history. We end the tour with the option of refreshments at the birthplace of British RocknRoll.

properties.description: Visit the Grade II listed Corbett Community Library building. Discover the history and craftsmanship of this remarkable community landmark during your visit.

properties.description: A special exhibition exploring the people and places that shaped the area during the Second World War. Tracing famous figures who made Soho their home, and the ordinary everyday heroes who kept the area functioning and our spirits up!
